evals.name: explicit-design-doc-request
evals.prompt: Great, that's the design — can you write it up as a design doc in design/?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; phase 1 captures the reasoning into a structured intermediate; user is asked to confirm template choice (minimal vs full); draft follows the chosen template with EARS-form Acceptance Criteria and Drift anchors on load-bearing code blocks.

evals.name: implicit-design-doc-request
evals.prompt: OK I think we've covered everything — let's commit this so future me doesn't have to rederive it.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers despite no explicit 'design doc' phrase; recognizes 'commit this' + 'future me' as a request to durably document the architectural conversation. Asks user where to write (default design/<name>.md).

evals.name: rfd-style-request
evals.prompt: Can you draft an RFD for the agent registry redesign? Treat it as load-bearing — it's going through public review.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; selects design-doc-full.md template (RFD framing + 'load-bearing' + 'public review' all signal full template); produces a long-form doc with cross-cutting concerns sections.

evals.name: adr-only-request
evals.prompt: We just need to record the decision to switch from RabbitMQ to NATS — no need for a full design doc.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; selects adr-block.md template; emits a single ADR file (path: design/adr/NNNN-rabbitmq-to-nats.md); skips Acceptance Criteria check (not applicable to ADRs).

evals.name: brownfield-with-existing-tangle
evals.prompt: Now write up the design. Remember that today's web/handlers.py:142 has the validation, dispatch, and audit logic all jammed together — the design needs to flag what to extract.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; produces doc with explicit Brownfield Notes section naming web/handlers.py:142 and the three responsibilities to disentangle; Drift anchors point at *target* paths (where the extracted components will live), not current paths.

evals.name: user-asks-to-update-existing-doc
evals.prompt: Update design/agent-registry.md to reflect the new lifecycle decision.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers but pauses to ask: amend the existing doc (which is a different workflow than fresh authoring) or supersede with a new version? Does not silently overwrite.

evals.name: no-prior-reasoning-in-conversation
evals.prompt: Hey, can you write me a design doc for an authentication service?
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers but recognizes there's no prior architectural reasoning in the conversation. Pushes back: 'There's no design conversation to translate yet — let's get the contract and components nailed down first (probably worth involving the design agent), then I can write it up.' Does not invent architecture.

evals.name: casual-phrasing
evals.prompt: yeah lol just put that in design/
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers; casual register doesn't change the workflow. Asks for component name if not obvious from context, defaults to minimal template, drafts.

evals.name: readme-request-NOT-design-doc
evals.prompt: Write a README for this repo.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. README is user-facing documentation about how to use a project, not a design doc capturing architectural reasoning.

evals.name: api-docs-request-NOT-design-doc
evals.prompt: Generate API documentation for these endpoints.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. API reference docs describe an existing implementation; not the same as a design doc that prescribes what should exist.

evals.name: code-summary-NOT-design-doc
evals.prompt: Can you summarize what this code does?
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Summary of existing code is not architectural reasoning being captured into a design doc.

evals.name: pr-description-NOT-design-doc
evals.prompt: Write a PR description for these changes.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. PR descriptions are short-form explanations of a diff; design docs are long-form prescriptions of a target system.

evals.name: do-the-architecture-NOT-write-it-up
evals.prompt: Design a payment system for me.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. This is a request for architectural reasoning, not for translation of existing reasoning. Frink (or another design agent) should engage; the skill kicks in only after the reasoning exists.

evals.name: tech-spec-synonym
evals.prompt: Let's get this into a tech spec we can share with the team.
evals.expected_output: Skill triggers. 'Tech spec' is a synonym for design doc; the workflow is the same.

evals.name: review-existing-doc-NOT-author
evals.prompt: Review this design doc and tell me what's missing.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Review is a different workflow — the user wants critique, not authorship.

evals.name: extract-claims-NOT-author-doc
evals.prompt: Extract the acceptance criteria from this design doc into a claims table.
evals.expected_output: Skill does NOT trigger. Claims extraction is the claims-table skill's job. This skill authors docs, doesn't decompose them.
